 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER 9 08-08-2025 I.A. No. 02 of 2025 Heard Mr. Rajiv Ranjan Kr. Pandey, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr.
Abhay Kumar, learned APP for the State.
2. The present Interlocutory Application has been placed for consideration of appellant's bail prayer and suspension of his sentence during the pendency of this appeal.
3. This appeal has been filed against the judgment of conviction dated 24.11.2022 and order of sentence dated 07.12.2022 passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act, Samastipur in connection with Trial No. 193 of 2022, arising out of N.H.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1353 of 2023(9) dt.08-08-2025 Bangra PS Case No. 05 of 2021,
whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366A and 376 of the IPC and under Section 4 of the POCSO Act and sentenced for the said offences.
4.

The main submissions advanced by the appellant's counsel are that the major punishment awarded upon the appellant is 10 years of R.I. for the offence punishable under section 4 of the POCSO Act against which he has served about four years and six months in jail and though his earlier prayer has been rejected on merit by this court vide order dated 03.01.2024 but now, the Sujit Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157892024/

sentences.text: appellant has renewed his prayer mainly on the ground of his incarceration period in jail and further, unlikelihood of his appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future as his appeal relates to the year 2023.

5. Though, on merit, the learned APP appearing for the State has opposed the prayer of the appellant, however, in view of his incarceration period he submits that a lenient approach may be taken in respect of his prayer.
6. Heard both the sides and perused the relevant materials.
Though, against this appellant, there is serious allegation and his earlier prayer has been rejected on merit, however, considering his present custody period, which is about Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.1353 of 2023(9)
dt.08-08-2025 four years and six months against the major punishment of 10 years of R. I. awarded upon him under section 4 of the POCSO Act

and in the present scenario of hearing of Cr. Appeals (SJ) in which the appellants are in jail by the Cr. Appeal (SJ) benches of this court, there is less possibility of hearing of the appellant's appeal in near future, in my opinion, in the said circumstances, the appellant now deserves to a lenient approach of this court.

Accordingly, let the appellant above-named be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- ( Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act,
Samastipur in connection with Trial No. 193 of 2022, arising out of N.H. Bangra PS Case No. 05 of 2021.
